newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

About 9,000 army deserters return to duty ahead of the government's amnesty which expired last week. Some 15,000 have deserted the security forces during past five years as war with separatist Tamil guerrillas escalated.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga returns on Monday after official visit to France.
Sri Lanka's first woman judge of the Supreme Court Professor Shiranee Bandaranayake, starts sitting on Monday.
Three petitioners file fundamental rights violation applications challenging Bandaranayake's appointment to the Supreme Court.
Police take into custody 17 suspected hard core Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas, including five women, who were allegedly sent to Colombo for suicide attacks on key targets.
Angry high school students in Kandy burn bus after it ran over 13-year-old sutdent at pedestrian crossing, killing him.
Three-months maternity leave plus 3,000 rupees per child birth for women employees of the state sector.

Five Tamil political parties to meet President Kumaratunga in bid to get upcoming local government elections in northern province postponed. They say situation in north is still unstable for peaceful election.
Sinhalese, Tamil and Moslem students in the south plan peace march in Galle town on December 9 to show national harmony.
